issues.title: feat(tui): add Vim WORD motions
issues.body:
TLDR: Bumping the useful vim mode with a few more motions that I commonly use and miss.

## What

Adds Vim's `W`, `B`, and `E` whitespace-delimited WORD motions, including counts, operator forms, Visual selections, punctuation-containing WORDs, and movement across line boundaries. The change is deliberately limited to these three motions.

## Why

The Vim editor already supports lowercase `w`, `b`, and `e`, but the corresponding WORD motions are missing. This makes common navigation over paths, flags, and punctuation-heavy text unnecessarily granular.

## Testing

- Launched the actual CLI with Vim mode enabled. On `foo-bar baz.qux`, `W` moved to `baz.qux`, `E` moved to its final grapheme, and `B` returned to its start.
- Exercised counted operator behavior with `d3W`; `a-b c.d e:f keep` became `keep`, and undo restored the original prompt.
- Exercised the reviewed multiline operator path in the actual CLI; `foo\nbar` with `dW` became `bar` without leaving an empty line.
- `bun test packages/tui/test/editor-vim.test.ts`: 70 passed, 0 failed.
- `bun run check:ts`: passed for every workspace package. One pre-existing unused-import warning remains in `packages/catalog/test/cline-pass-compat.test.ts`.
- `bun check`: TypeScript checks passed; the Rust check could not start because `cargo` is not installed on this workstation.

---

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] CHANGELOG updated with the required attribution (if user-facing; internal issue fixes use issue links, external contributions add the PR link and contributor credit after creation)

issues.title: feat(tui): frame fenced Markdown code blocks
issues.body:
## What

Render completed fenced Markdown blocks in compact, width-aware frames while preserving source whitespace, list and quote container geometry, wide graphemes, optional language/copy labels, and open-fence streaming stability. Incremental rendering also reuses append-only guard scans and resumes stable-block discovery after the frozen prefix.

This cleanly attributed branch replaces #9513. It was rebuilt from the final reviewed tree on top of `upstream/main` without rewriting any public branch. All review fixes from #9513 are included, plus the final copy-span fix that anchors fenced payload recovery after preceding HTML/prose tokens.

## Why

Long streamed responses repeatedly scanned the growing Markdown tail and revisited stable prefix tokens. Completed fenced code also needed a structured layout that survives narrow terminals, nested lists, blockquotes, ANSI highlighting, raw tab-preserving copy payloads, duplicate normalized fences, and terminal hyperlink capability changes.

## Testing

- **219 passed, 0 failed:** focused Markdown and coding-agent Mermaid contracts
- **1324 passed, 0 failed:** complete `packages/tui` suite
- **`bun check` passed:** full TypeScript/Biome and Rust workspace checks under pinned Bun 1.4.0
- Copy-span regression covers fence-like HTML/prose before the rendered fence

issues.title: fix(launch): answer terminal queries in broker ptys
issues.body:
## Repro

Start a supervised PTY with `hub start` whose child enters raw mode, writes `ESC[6n`, and exits only after receiving `ESC[row;colR`; then run `hub send` with text and Enter. Both sends report success, but before this change `hub describe` continues to show the child alive because no terminal response reaches it.

## Cause

`DaemonBroker.#launchPty` in `packages/coding-agent/src/launch/broker.ts` advertised `TERM=xterm-256color` and fixed dimensions, but sent each PTY output chunk directly to the log without a terminal parser, so DSR and DA queries had no terminal-side responder.

## Fix

- Feed supervised PTY output through the shared headless `Terminal` at the broker's fixed dimensions.
- Write terminal-generated replies back to the same PTY session and dispose the parser when that generation settles.
- Cover a raw-mode DSR probe with a broker integration regression and document the user-visible fix in the changelog.

## Verification

`bun test packages/coding-agent/test/launch/broker-output-snapshot.test.ts` passes (2 tests), `bun run --cwd packages/coding-agent check:types` passes, and the pre-publish `bun check` gate passes.

Fixes #10573

issues.title: feat(coding-agent): add confidential terminal input helper
issues.body:
## What

- Add a reusable confidential terminal-input helper for future TUI, setup, and RPC credential flows.
- Require exclusive ownership of a raw-mode TTY and fail closed when echo suppression is unavailable.
- Reject concurrent or shared input consumers, restore terminal mode and stream flow on every exit path, and expose the helper through root and subpath exports.

## Why

#5281 needs a shared no-echo primitive before API-key login can be added consistently across surfaces. This prerequisite keeps terminal state and secret-input guarantees in one implementation without changing any active login flow.

## Testing

- `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/cli/secret-input.test.ts`
- `cd packages/coding-agent && bun run check`
- Exercised two sequential prompts through a real PTY. Only prompt labels and returned lengths appeared in output; entered values did not.

issues.title: fix(tui): render tool-call payload echoes byte-verbatim
issues.body:
Tool-call echo cards were mangling the payloads they display: `$(grep -c X $P)` came back as `(grep -c X P)` — dollar sigils just gone — `A_rows` turned into `Aᵣows` with a subscripted `r`, and a five-line command collapsed into one re-wrapped blob. On a debugging surface that's bad news, so I traced it and fixed it.

## What

Tool-call payload echoes — bash `command`, write file content, `eval` `code`/cell source, `read` file content — render byte-verbatim instead of passing through the markdown/LaTeX typesetter and the card's prose wrapper, with every byte of an overflowing row recoverable on screen. Task brief/context (`task`/`context`) keep their markdown typesetting through a new literal-math mode on the Markdown renderer: headings/lists/code/links read as prose while `$…$`, `$$…$$` and `\(...\)` spans stay byte-literal.

There were two corruption paths:

1. **The typesetter mutating parameters.** The task tool fed its raw `task`/`context` parameters into `new Markdown(...)`. An inline `$$` pair (say, the shell-PID idiom `pid=$$`) opens a math span whose closer search has no anti-currency or newline guards, so a multi-line brief gets swallowed into one math body and rendered by `latexToUnicode` — which eats `$…$` sigils as TeX toggles, subscript-converts `_r`, and collapses newlines to spaces. BRE groups like `grep "\(A_rows\)"` hit the same subscript conversion through `\(...\)`.
2. **The frame's prose wrap.** `renderOutputBlock` ran `wrapTextWithAnsi(line.trimEnd(), …)` over every framed card body line, so long command lines broke at width-dependent points (indistinguishable from real newlines) and trailing whitespace disappeared.

The fix treats payload echoes as payloads, not prose (which is what the repo's sanitization convention implies anyway — `sanitizeText` / `sanitizeDisplayLines` normalize display safety, never content):

- `OutputBlockOptions` / `ToolCardSection` gained a `verbatim` flag with a recoverable-overflow contract: `expanded` (ctrl+o) chunks each source line across rows whose continuation rows carry a dim `↪` gutter marker — a soft wrap can never read as a payload newline — and collapsed clips to a byte-prefix with a visible `…` marker, so a cut is never silent and the rest is one expand away. Chunks are strict column slices, so cuts land on grapheme/ANSI boundaries and concatenating the rows minus their markers re-joins the source line byte-for-byte. It's honored by both card variants (framed and plain) and set on the bash command echo (call + result), the write file-content echo (call + result), and the code-cell source section — which covers `eval` `code` and the `read`/read-group file-content echoes too.
- Task brief/context render through `createMarkdownSectionRenderer` and the Markdown renderer's new opt-in **literal-math mode**. Structure typesets (`## Goal` renders as a heading, lists/code/links work), but the payload-mutation paths are gone: no `mathSpanAt` consumption, no `latexToUnicode`, no `\(...\)` BRE-group conversion, no `_r`-style subscript mapping, no math smart-punct — and a literal-escape inline rule keeps backslash-escaped punctuation's bytes instead of smartening `\(` away. So `pid=$$`, `$(grep -c A_rows $P)`, `A_rows`, and `grep "\(A_rows\)" $P` all appear verbatim inside the rendered brief rows. Long single-line paragraphs wrap across rows (soft wraps in prose are normal and unambiguous there) instead of clipping. Every other markdown surface — `read` markdown results, `eval` markdown output, execution output sections, `ask`, `think`, assistant/user prose — keeps its current rendering.
- Task brief/context `\r` runs follow the parameter convention (`sanitizeCarriageReturns`: word separators), not the subprocess progress-overwrite convention, so `Retry\rnow` echoes both words. `sanitizeCarriageReturns` has to run before `sanitizeText`, which otherwise drops `\r` outright and merges the words around it.
- `sanitizeDisplayLines` drops exactly one trailing empty row — the split artifact past a final `\n`/`\r\n` — instead of every trailing empty row: `"foo\n\n"` keeps its one real blank line, `"\n\n"` keeps its two rows, and a trailing lone `\r` (a progress overwrite, not a terminator) keeps its final segment row (`"50%\r"` stays `[""]`).

Genuinely-markdown content keeps its typesetting: `read` markdown results, `eval` markdown output, execution output sections, and the human-facing surfaces (`ask` questions/labels, `think` scratchpad, assistant/user prose). One surface I noticed but left alone: `ask` option labels go through `renderInlineMarkdown` and could hit the same `_r`/math mutation, but labels are presentation prose this PR deliberately keeps typeset — flagging it for a follow-up.

## Review notes (second round)

**Blocking, `output-block.ts:154` — silent clipping, `expanded` ignored.** Fixed at the suggested bar and above: expanded wraps fully into `↪`-marked continuation rows, collapsed clips with a visible `…`. The exact smoke command at width 80 (literal output of `bashToolRenderer.renderCall` at the test frame width, both modes):

```text
--- expanded:true
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ $ cd packages/coding-agent && bun test … 2>&1 | grep -E 'fail|error' ; echo  │
│ ↪ EXIT_MARKER=$?                                                             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
--- expanded:false
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ $ cd packages/coding-agent && bun test … 2>&1 | grep -E 'fail|error' ; echo… │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Expanded row 1 matches the shape of the reviewer's own captured output on this head's predecessor (the command through `; echo`, then a hard row end) — there the card just ended with nothing after it and no sign of a cut; for this payload the old render clipped at exactly `; echo ` in both modes. Now the tail sits on a marker-delimited continuation row and `EXIT_MARKER=$?` is on screen, and collapsed announces its cut with `…`.

**Blocking, `task.ts:586` — briefs lost typesetting; suggested fixing the `$$` delimiter scanner in `packages/utils/src/math-delimiters.ts` instead.** The maintainer decision landed on a third path: briefs regain markdown typesetting through the renderer's opt-in literal-math mode rather than changing the shared delimiter grammar. A scanner-level `$$` guard would change every markdown surface at once (assistant prose included) and can't be validated by this PR's tests; the mode is opt-in and scoped to brief/context, and the `math-delimiters` guard remains a good standalone follow-up. The comment's smoke claim is addressed — `## Goal\nInvestigate why … keeps the JSONL append atomic. END_OF_PARAGRAPH\n\n- Read …` at width 80, identical in `expanded: false` and `expanded: true`:

```text
╭─── ⇶ Task ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Goal                                                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ Investigate why the session persistence layer the session persistence layer  │
│ the session persistence layer the session persistence layer the session      │
│ persistence layer the session persistence layer keeps the JSONL append       │
│ atomic. END_OF_PARAGRAPH                                                     │
│                                                                              │
│ - Read the store.                                                            │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ • Sam: ## Goal                                                               │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

`Goal` is a typeset heading, the paragraph wraps in full (`END_OF_PARAGRAPH` on screen — previously clipped away in both modes), and the list renders. The nit is addressed too: the section renderer consumes `width` again (it renders at the frame's inner width), so the `(width) => …` indirection is alive.

**Should-fix, `render-utils.ts:405` — over-pop and shared-helper blast radius.** Gone: exactly one element is popped, and only after a final `\n`/`\r\n` — `"foo\n\n"` → `["foo", ""]`, `"\n\n"` → `["", ""]`, `"50%\r"` → `[""]`. On placement: with briefs back on markdown there is no verbatim renderer left to own a local pop, and `"foo\n\n"` → `["foo", ""]` is exactly the "pop exactly one element" option the review listed as acceptable — the value the review's own "one row plus one real blank line" reading demands. The `read`/`fetch` echoes now see only the phantom-artifact removal (their trailing terminator no longer yields a blank row), never a real blank row being eaten.

**Should-fix, `verbatim-tool-payload-echo.test.ts:149` — tests locking in byte loss.** Rewritten to the recoverable contract: expanded shows every byte of the 204-char line across marked continuation rows, collapsed shows the clip marker, and the rows minus their markers re-join the source line (the code-cell, write call/result, and plain-card variants all covered). The `$$`/`A_rows` assertions are kept as regression coverage, and new cases cover grapheme/ANSI cut boundaries and the exact smoke command at width 80 in both modes.

The review's open question — wrap with marked continuation rows or clip — is resolved as: wrap with marked rows when expanded, clip with a visible marker when collapsed.

## Why

An echo card is how you verify what ran or what was dispatched. Any echo that can silently differ from the payload is a correctness problem — and the same typesetter path could mangle identifiers, paths, or code quoted inside a brief. The observed fingerprints in the wild were exactly the ones above. The overflow side of the contract follows the same rule: bytes you cannot reach are bytes you cannot verify, so the expanded view must show the whole payload and the collapsed view must say it cut.

## Testing

`packages/tui/test/verbatim-tool-payload-echo.test.ts` renders a synthetic payload (`pid=$$`, `run: $(grep -c A_rows $P)`, `grep "\(A_rows\)" $P`, a 424-char line, `done $$`) through the real `taskToolRenderer.renderCall` and `bashToolRenderer.renderCall` cards and asserts byte-identical rows. Coverage adds CR-separated brief words, brief structure typesetting next to literal payload bytes, the wrapped brief smoke, write call/result echoes, the code-cell source echo, plain-variant `verbatim` forwarding, grapheme/ANSI cut boundaries, the recoverable-overflow contract on the 204-char line, and the exact reviewer smoke command at width 80.

Red before each fix (fix-only reverse-apply: source hunks dropped, tests kept):

- Recoverable overflow: 6 fail / 5 pass — every 204-char recovery test plus the smoke rejected the marker-less clip; the smoke at `expanded: true` showed exactly the reviewer's clipped single row.
- Literal-math briefs: 2 fail / 11 pass — the structure test saw `## Goal` untyped-set behind raw text and the brief smoke's `END_OF_PARAGRAPH` missing (verbatim rows at frame width).
- `sanitizeDisplayLines`: 2 fail / 44 pass — `["foo", ""]` came back `["foo"]`, `["", ""]` came back `[]`, `[""]` came back `[]`.

All green after. Every fix was red/green'd individually (reverse just that fix's src hunks, keep its tests, observe the concrete wrong output, restore). One test-design note: the "byte-identical when it fits" bash test originally passed even with the fix removed — plain trailing spaces get absorbed by the frame's padding and highlighted runs end in an SGR code where `trimEnd` is a no-op — so it uses a whitespace-only row with U+00A0 blanks that only the verbatim path preserves.

Gates (every number from a run on my machine):

- `bun run check` from `packages/tui` (the covering gate — everything in this diff lives there): pass, format-clean + clean `tsgo`.
- `env -u CI HOME=$(mktemp -d) bun run test` from `packages/coding-agent`: 172/178 chunk commands `(ok, …)` (two full runs; 6 chunks failed in each). Every failure is the known real-Puppeteer load-flake class (Puppeteer tests hitting their 30s timeouts under parallel Chromium and, in one run, a 600s chunk watchdog kill) plus one unit flake (`test/agent-session-retry-fallback.test.ts`); each failing file passes standalone on this same tree (`browser-freeze-settle` 41/41 in 292s, `agent-session-retry-fallback` 103/103). The failing tests import no `pi-tui` code, so this diff (all `packages/tui`) cannot reach them — labeled known-INFRA per the browser-flake policy. (`CI` must be unset — the ambient shell exports `CI=true`, which flips the runner to its fail-fast path.)
- Full `packages/tui` suite: `2887 pass / 5 skip / 0 fail`, `Ran 2892 tests across 224 files`. The `terminal-capabilities` tmux intermittent did not fire.
- Environment note: `acp-builtins.test.ts` "/mcp resources" fails under a default `$HOME` that has ambient MCP config (it expects "No MCP servers configured") and passes 83/83 under an isolated `$HOME`. Intermittent, observed on the unmodified tree too: `terminal-capabilities.test.ts` "uses the attached client's terminal profile" — passes on rerun and standalone.
- This diff changes no files under `collab-web/`, so `gen:tool-views` output is unaffected. Verification is rendered-component level (the changed surface is the tool card renderer), not a live interactive session.

## CHANGELOG

Entry under `packages/tui/CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` → `### Fixed`, one user-visible line, with the PR link and credit appended in this branch.

issues.title: feat(tui): support option-clicking in prompt entry box to move cursor
issues.body:
## What

Moves the prompt caret to the clicked character on Option-click, for terminals where `tui.mouse` click capture is enabled.

- `packages/tui/src/mouse.ts`: `SgrMouseEvent` now decodes the `shift`/`alt`/`ctrl` bits the button code already carried (4/8/16), so an Option-click is identifiable as an ordinary left press with `alt` set.
- `packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts`: adds `setViewportPaintRow(row)` plus `placeCursorAtViewportCell(rowInViewport, col)`. The latter maps a pointer cell to a buffer position using the same chrome widths and wrapped rows the last `render` painted — wrapped segments resolve to their own buffer offset, cells past a row clamp to that row's end, atomic placeholder tokens snap to the nearer edge, and normal-mode Vim rests the caret on a grapheme. It moves only the caret and reports no document mutation.
- `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/composer.ts`: publishes the editor's **signed** row within the painted mutable viewport each frame, measured during the pass that already renders the rows (no component is rendered twice). The row stays negative when the editor's top is clipped above the viewport, so its lower rows remain addressable.
- `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/input-controller.ts`: routes Option-clicks in `#handleInlineMouse` to the editor and repaints. Plain clicks keep focusing live subagent cards; the editor rejects rows outside its own painted ones, so the two never compete.
- `packages/coding-agent/src/config/settings-schema.ts`: `tui.mouse`'s description now names Option-click caret placement alongside click-to-focus.

## Why

While `tui.mouse` capture is on, every SGR report is consumed, so the terminal no longer performs its native Option-click caret placement and the prompt box had no way to move the caret with the mouse. This restores the shell-prompt gesture inside the composer. With capture off (the default) nothing changes: no reporting is requested and the terminal keeps its native Shift+drag selection and Option-click behavior.

## Testing

- `packages/tui`: full suite **1547 pass / 0 fail**. New cases cover modifier-bit decoding, cell→column mapping, multi-line row selection, end-of-row and left-of-text clamping, wrapped-segment offsets, atomic-token snapping, clipped (negative) paint rows, unpainted rows being refused, no-`onChange`, and the Vim normal/insert caret rules.
- `packages/coding-agent`: the click-routing suite drives a real `CustomEditor` through the real `InputController` and asserts the caret actually moves and repaints while no agent is focused, that a further-right cell lands further right, that the click is rebased onto the published viewport top, and that an unpaintable viewport (resize transaction) places nothing. **71 pass / 0 fail** across the six affected suites; the singleton/global-state bucket is **890 pass / 2 skip**.
- `bun run check:ts`: clean across every workspace package.
- **Pre-existing, unrelated:** `test/git-tui-sidebar.test.ts` fails 4 cases on this base. I confirmed it reproduces with this branch's changes stashed, i.e. on pristine `origin/main`.

Improve `/usage` with provider/account cards, account merge/split controls, optional account-label masking, and configurable quota-bar labels. Keep activity and detail views available, including organization-qualified account labels and deduplicated notes.

Privacy and grouping toggles apply to the current overlay without silently changing saved configuration. Closing the dashboard still cancels activity loading through its AbortSignal.
